HEADLINE: Gabon says access to social media restored after eight-month ban

A SMALL, CLEAN, FULLY SOURCED ITEM. Use it only if you need a fifth that costs you nothing on the theme ceiling and carries no casualty figures to label.

HARD FACTS
- Gabon has lifted a ban on social media imposed EIGHT MONTHS ago.
- The High Communication Authority (HAC) announced the reversal ON SATURDAY in a televised statement.
- "The BBC has approached the country's media regulator for comment." NO COMMENT RECEIVED — so there is no second voice in this piece at all.
- The ban was introduced on 17 FEBRUARY, with the HAC saying online content was fuelling conflict and deepening divisions.
- Gabon has a population of about 2.5 million.
- Platforms affected and named: Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram. Many people turned to VPNs to keep access.
- The ban was imposed while President Brice Oligui Nguema faced "a wave of social unrest less than a year after his election". Teachers and civil servants had struck over what they said were low pay and poor working conditions.
- The opposition said the suspension was an abuse of power. THE OPPOSITION IS NOT NAMED. Do not attribute to a named party.
- Nguema won last year's elections with MORE THAN 90% of the vote, two years after his coup ended more than five decades of rule by the Bongo family.
- He had pledged to reform Gabon, "a small, oil- and timber-rich country, where digital blackouts were used by the previous governments to control information".

NO NAMED INDIVIDUAL IS QUOTED ANYWHERE IN THIS PIECE. There is no direct quotation at all beyond the HAC's reasoning paraphrased. If your format requires a named quote, this item cannot supply one.
